A 33-year-old male underwent a pre-employment medical check-up and was found to have an elevated SGPT (ALT) of 194. He reports that the rest of the evaluation was normal, including CBC, ESR, liver tests (other than SGPT), urine routine, blood group/Rh factor, chest X-ray, general physical examination, fasting and postprandial blood sugar, total cholesterol, ECG, and serum creatinine. He was advised to obtain a full-abdomen ultrasound, which was completed and reported as normal except for mild fatty liver.

He reports a recent episode of loose stools for which he took ofloxacin 200 mg with ornidazole 500 mg twice daily for 2 days, then continued ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily for another 3 days; he notes he also had cold and cough during this time. He reports he is not a heavy drinker and drinks only occasionally, and he does not frequently eat junk food.

He asks what could be the reason for the elevated SGPT, whether he is likely to receive medical clearance to join a new company, what he should do to lower SGPT levels, and what diet he should follow.
